WITH manager_throws AS (
  SELECT 
    p.throws,
    COUNT(*) AS tally
  FROM manager_award ma
  JOIN player p ON ma.player_id = p.player_id
  GROUP BY p.throws
),
totals AS (
  SELECT 
    SUM(tally) AS total_tally,
    COUNT(*) AS num_hands
  FROM manager_throws
),
avg_share_value AS (
  SELECT 
    1.0 / num_hands AS avg_share
  FROM totals
),
hand_shares AS (
  SELECT 
    throws,
    tally,
    CAST(tally AS FLOAT) / (SELECT total_tally FROM totals) AS share
  FROM manager_throws
),
above_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    throws,
    tally,
    share
  FROM hand_shares
  WHERE share > (SELECT avg_share FROM avg_share_value)
)
SELECT 
  SUM(tally) AS combined_tally,
  CAST(SUM(tally) AS FLOAT) / (SELECT total_tally FROM totals) AS their_average_share,
  CAST(SUM(tally) AS FLOAT) / (SELECT total_tally FROM totals) - (SELECT avg_share FROM avg_share_value) AS how_far_above
FROM above_avg;

assumptions.assumption: "Manager award winners" refers to rows in manager_award; unmatched rows (those without a player in the player table) are dropped via INNER JOIN.
"Average share" is the share-per-group if all groups were equal: 1 / number_of_distinct_throwing_hands.
NULL values in throws are treated as a distinct group (not excluded).
"How far above the average share they sit on average" refers to the combined share (of all above-average hands) minus the per-group average share.

alternatives.interpretation: "Their average share" and "how far above the average share they sit on average" refer to unweighted averages of the individual hands' shares, not the combined group share. That is: the average of the shares of hands above average, and the average of their individual exceedances above the per-group average.
